hero.title: Nourishing children and families across Metro Manila.
hero.text: Oksyo is a community-led feeding initiative working to bring balanced, locally sourced meals to children and families who need them, guided by one promise: walang iwanan, no one left behind.

glance.label: Initial focus areas in Metro Manila

about.label: Who we are
about.title: A community initiative built on care, not charity from a distance.
paragraphs: Oksyo was founded by John Harold Mejia, an Information Technology student at Angeles University Foundation, with a simple belief: a nourishing meal is the foundation for a child's energy to learn, play, and grow.
We work alongside local leaders, volunteers, and community partners so that every meal day is shaped by the people it serves. We listen first, plan together, and keep food support close to home.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.text: To provide safe, balanced, and dignified meal support to children and families in Metro Manila, using local ingredients and community partnerships.

vision.title: Our vision
vision.text: A community where no child goes to school or to sleep hungry, and where neighbors look out for one another.

why.label: Why it matters
why.title: Food is more than a meal.
why.text: Regular, nutritious food supports a child's focus in class, physical growth, and overall well-being. For many families in dense urban communities, rising food costs and unstable income make consistent meals hard to guarantee. Community feeding fills that gap with practical, immediate care.

points.title: Energy to learn
points.text: Children concentrate better and take part more fully when they are not hungry.

points.title: Healthy growth
points.text: Balanced meals with rice, vegetables, and protein support growing bodies.

points.title: Stronger community
points.text: Shared meals build trust and remind families that their neighbors care.

programs.label: Our programs
programs.title: What Oksyo does.
programs.intro: Four connected activities make up the Community Feeding Program.

items.title: Community meal days
items.text: Planned, volunteer-supported meal days that serve filling, balanced food to children and families at safe, agreed distribution points.

items.title: Local sourcing
items.text: We aim to buy ingredients from nearby suppliers and markets, supporting local livelihoods while keeping food fresh.

items.title: Partner referrals
items.text: We work with barangay leaders, schools, and community groups to understand who needs support and where.

items.title: Volunteer network
items.text: Students, professionals, and neighbors can help with preparation, serving, logistics, and documentation.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Speak with local leaders and families to understand needs, dietary concerns, and the best day and place to serve.

steps.title: Plan the menu
steps.text: Design balanced, affordable meals and confirm quantities with each community partner.

steps.title: Source locally
steps.text: Buy fresh ingredients from nearby suppliers wherever practical.

steps.title: Prepare safely
steps.text: Follow safe food-handling practices with trained volunteers and clean, reusable supplies where possible.

steps.title: Serve with dignity
steps.text: Distribute meals in an orderly, respectful way, so everyone is welcomed and no one is singled out.

focusAreas.label: Where we hope to serve
focusAreas.title: Start local. Listen first.

items.name: Payatas

items.name: Nearby communities
items.text: Additional locations can be shaped around partner referrals, volunteer capacity, and local priorities.

items.title: Dignity
items.text: Everyone is served with respect. Food support should never feel like a favor.

items.title: Transparency
items.text: We are open about what we plan, what we know, and what is still being confirmed.

items.title: Local first
items.text: Local ingredients, local partners, and local leadership shape each meal day.

items.title: Safety
items.text: Safe food handling and child-friendly practices come before everything else.

usage.label: Your contribution
usage.title: How your gift is used.
usage.text: Donations are directed toward the practical costs of running a meal day. Amounts are suggestions, not a guaranteed number of meals, and we confirm arrangements with donors directly.

items.title: Ingredients
items.text: Rice, vegetables, protein, and other staples from local suppliers.

items.title: Preparation supplies
items.text: Cooking essentials, food-safe containers, and reusable serving items.

items.title: Delivery and logistics
items.text: Transport and coordination to get meals to the people who need them.

items.title: Listen and connect
items.text: Hold community conversations and build relationships with local leaders and partner groups.

items.title: Plan and prepare
items.text: Finalize menus, sourcing, food-safety steps, and volunteer teams for a first meal day.

items.title: Serve
items.text: Run community meal days with partner communities and gather feedback.

items.title: Report and grow
items.text: Share what we learned and expand to more communities in a responsible way.

involved.label: Get involved
involved.title: There is a place for everyone.

items.title: Donate
items.text: Give a one-time gift securely online to support ingredients and meal preparation.

items.title: Volunteer
items.text: Offer your time for meal preparation, serving, logistics, or documentation.

items.title: Partner with us
items.text: Schools, barangays, businesses, and community groups can help us reach families.

items.a: Oksyo was founded by John Harold Mejia, an Information Technology student at Angeles University Foundation. You can read more on the About page.

items.q: Are the focus areas confirmed feeding sites?
items.a: Not yet. The areas shown are illustrative starting points for community conversations. Locations, dates, and distribution points will be confirmed together with local leaders and partners.

items.q: Are the photos from Oksyo activities?
items.a: No. Photos on this site are illustrative community imagery and are not documentation of Oksyo feeding activities.
Payments are processed by Stripe. Your card details are entered into Stripe's secure form, and Oksyo does not receive or store them.
Monthly giving is not available yet. At the moment we accept one-time donations in Philippine pesos, starting from ₱100.
You will receive an email confirmation after your payment. If you need documentation for your records, please contact us directly.
